Energy has been centre stage at #Davos this week. And, amid all of this: AI. AI is not artificial. It has a long tail of energy-hungry physical data centres and GPU racks, critical mineral mining, and real-world inference demanding unprecedented power supplies.

So, how do we harness these two seemingly separate but, in reality, interconnected and intertwined revolutions - the energy transition, and the AI era? This is the focus of our new Bulletin, below, where we define the ‘digital energy stack’.

In the tech world, a ’stack’ is the collection of different technologies and components needed for a digital product or service to function. As you read this post, it sits on a ’stack’ of solutions: a web browser or LinkedIn application on your phone or other device. Internet and email protocols that (hopefully!) are displaying the below graphic and link correctly. And, layers of cloud hosting, connectivity, and - of course - energy, to make all of this happen.

We are applying this ‘stack’ approach to sustainable energy. We need a systems-level approach, and coherent and strategic efforts. There are seven elements in the ’digital energy stack’:

📊 𝐃𝐚𝐭𝐚 - the 'fuel' of the energy revolution. Big, Lean, and Thick Data.
📱 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐧𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐯𝐢𝐭𝐲 - including 3G and 4G, and IoT.
🖥️ 𝐂𝐨𝐦𝐩𝐮𝐭𝐞 - the 'currency' of the 21st century.
🪪 𝐃𝐢𝐠𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐏𝐮𝐛𝐥𝐢𝐜 𝐈𝐧𝐟𝐫𝐚𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐮𝐜𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞 - to amplify the impact of inclusive energy.
🔒 𝐂𝐲𝐛𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐞𝐜𝐮𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐲 - recognising energy's status as critical national infrastructure. 
🤖 𝐀𝐈 - with AI driving new energy solutions, but also creating new challenges.
🏛️ 𝐆𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐧𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞 - shaping the talent, culture, and  institutions of the energy transition.

Importantly, there is no single pathway for any of these seven components. Digital and energy innovation is occurring and emerging everywhere, from Silicon Valley to the Silicon Savannah. The Global South is not just an innovation taker - but a maker, and shaper.

Without intentional design, digital risks reinforcing and entrenching energy inequality rather than accelerating an inclusive and just energy transition. The question is no longer whether AI and energy will intersect. It is whether we design that intersection to deliver development, resilience, and equity at scale.
